topic: Introduction to other method of expressing positions i.e. pin points, range and bearing.
syllabus_extract: Introduction to other method of expressing positions i.e. pin points, range and bearing.
specific_objectives: 14.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain and define a position on the earth.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Plotting range and bearing on chart; Safety: Handle chart paper carefully; Supervision: Instructor monitors plotting accuracy.
intro_questions: What are the primary methods used to define a position on the earth?
Why is it necessary to use alternative methods besides latitude and longitude?
Can you recall any military applications for range and bearing?

development.content:
Definition of Pin Point
Concept of Range
Concept of Bearing
Relationship between Range and Bearing
Importance in Navigation

Methods of expressing position
Pin point coordinates
Range measurement techniques
Bearing determination
Combined range and bearing usage

Accuracy considerations
Error sources in measurement
Standard notation formats
Application scenarios
Comparison with Lat/Long

summary_questions: Define a pin point in the context of expressing position.
Explain how range and bearing are used together to locate an object.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on how the concepts of range and bearing will be utilized in the upcoming lesson on speed and velocity vectors.

pft_rows.syllabus: Introduction to speed and velocity, vectors, wind velocity, vector addition and triangle of velocity.
